title: Data-sharing specialists (score-level): per-arm domain-interaction fusion
question: Does letting the fusion weights depend on the row's domain (the score-level data-sharing proxy) recover specialist gains beyond M143b's flat stacking?

score_caches.note: the m143b train cache stores arm score matrices and labels only, NOT domains; domain indicators for the interaction features are taken from the corpus train_domains (the M141 schedule's first 138k rows) and test_domains.

cell.interaction: each arm's 345-dim score vector GATED per domain (7 arms x 6 domains = 42 gated copies, 14,490 features) appended to the flat 7-arm concat (2,415) => 16,905 fusion features; the row's domain one-hot selects which copy is active, so the fusion weights may depend on the row's domain; fusion = stacking with the M143b valid-slice protocol.
cell.note: the registered interpretation of score-level data sharing; head-level sharing stays M159.

gate.registered: fused(interaction) >= global + 0.005 on the sealed test scores, else archived as a scoped negative.
